story.title: The Stage Cleaner
story.logline: A woman who sanitizes crime scenes before they happen realizes her job isn't cleaning up violence—it's planting the psychological triggers that cause it.
story.twist: The cleaning company does not scrub away evidence; it stages gruesome crime scenes in advance to manipulate innocent residents into committing murder.
story.ending: Maya succumbs to the psychological prompt staged in her own home, echoing the opening hook with a terrifying realization.

scenes.narration: I get paid to clean crime scenes before the bodies even hit the floor. My employer sends coordinates, I scrub the blood.
scenes.visual_prompt: Vertical shot, Maya, a 28-year-old woman with a short dark bob wearing a sleek silver biohazard suit, kneeling in a dimly lit modern apartment, scrubbing fluorescent liquid into dark hardwood floors.

scenes.narration: It sounds impossible, but the system is relentless. Every detail must match the work order perfectly down to the final smudge.
scenes.visual_prompt: Vertical shot, Maya, a 28-year-old woman with a short dark bob in a silver biohazard suit, checking glowing red numbers on a sleek black digital tablet in a dark rain-slicked alleyway.

scenes.narration: Tonight, a new assignment pops onto my tablet. I open the file, and my heart drops into my hollow stomach.
scenes.visual_prompt: Vertical shot, Maya, a 28-year-old woman with a short dark bob in a silver biohazard suit, looking terrified as the illuminated tablet screen casts a pale glow on her face inside a service van.

scenes.narration: The coordinates point directly to apartment 4B. That is my apartment. My safe space. My home.
scenes.visual_prompt: Vertical shot, Maya, a 28-year-old woman with a short dark bob in a silver biohazard suit, running up a narrow, dimly lit apartment hallway past door numbers 4A and 4B.

scenes.narration: I race through the rain, terrified I will find my sister shattered on the floor. I burst through the front door.
scenes.visual_prompt: Vertical shot, Maya, a 28-year-old woman with a short dark bob in a silver biohazard suit, pushing open a heavy door into her warm-lit, cozy modern living room with a beige rug.

scenes.narration: The apartment is completely empty except for a stranger wearing the exact same silver suit as me, holding a bucket.
scenes.visual_prompt: Vertical shot, Maya, a 28-year-old woman with a short dark bob in a silver biohazard suit, standing frozen at the doorway, staring at an older figure in an identical silver suit standing over the rug.

scenes.narration: He isn't scrubbing blood away. He is carefully spreading dark red paint onto the beige rug in precise streaks.
scenes.visual_prompt: Vertical shot, close up on the figure in a silver biohazard suit using a small brush to splash synthetic red liquid across Maya's beige living room rug.

scenes.narration: I drop my bleach bottle. He turns slowly, pointing at the work order. 'We don't clean past crimes, kid. We plant them.'
scenes.visual_prompt: Vertical shot, Maya, a 28-year-old woman with a short dark bob in a silver biohazard suit, dropping a plastic bottle as the older male cleaner hands her a glowing black tablet.

scenes.narration: The mind sees blood and creates a killer. Every scene I ever prepped was a subconscious prompt for a future victim.
scenes.visual_prompt: Vertical shot, Maya, a 28-year-old woman with a short dark bob in a silver biohazard suit, staring wide-eyed at her own reflection in a dark window pane inside her living room.

scenes.narration: Now I stare at the painted stain on my rug, feeling the urge grow. Who will clean up after me?
scenes.visual_prompt: Vertical shot, Maya, a 28-year-old woman with a short dark bob in a silver biohazard suit, standing alone in her living room looking down at the red stain on the rug with a cold expression.

caption.hook: She doesn't clean scenes, she creates them.
caption.title: The Stage Cleaner: A Scripted Tragedy
caption.caption: I spent years scrubbing floors, believing I was erasing sins. I never realized the bleach was just a primer for the nightmares I was ordered to plant. Is destiny something we face, or something we are staged to fulfill?
